answer: In an agent-run compute market serving a remote mesa, each identity must lock $100 for 30 days to receive a fixed daily bidding quota. The bond is an anchor for that quota: splitting into more accounts requires more locked capital, not merely more names. A cipher may conceal who controls those accounts, but it cannot reuse escrowed funds. An attacker seeking 1,000 identities must immobilize $100,000 and bear its financing cost for the lock period.
